newsitem.title: UK: Peugeot's UK workers ban overtime. [CORRECTED 16:53 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Peugeot's UK workers ban overtime. [CORRECTED 16:53 GMT]

text.p: British workers at French car-maker PSA Peugeot's Coventry plant have agreed to a ban on overtime from March 14 (corrects date from March 7) and will go on indefinite strike from March 21 onwards unless the company agrees to negotiate on pay and conditions, unions said on Thursday.

The Transport and General (T&G) told Reuters that company bosses had until March 21 to open talks or face all-out strike which could involve up to 3,000 British workers. The move follows overwhelming support for industrial action by Peugeot production line workers in a strike ballot.

The T&G published the results of its ballot on Wednesday which showed that 1,720 workers backed strike action, with 363 against. In a vote on other forms of industrial action, 1,848 were in favour, with 243 against.
The Coventry plant is Peugeot's only produciton facility in Britain and turned out 85,000 cars last year.
Union officials said workers had been forced into drastic measures because of frustration over a dispute centred on longer shifts and Peugeot's refusal to bring pay in line with other manufacturers.
The two sides have been in logjam since December and the dispute comes at a time when all car makers are facing tough sales and poor profits in Europe.

Analysts warn that Peugeot workers could be playing a dangerous game at a time when the industry is suffering from over-capacity. LMC International's director of motor research Charles Young said the Peugeot Coventry plant was known as a "low production and antiquated plant."

He added that it would not be difficult to boost capacity in Peugeot's more modern Spanish or French plants, if necessary. Peugeot itself was unavailable for immediate comment on the news. ($ = 0.620 British Pounds)
